[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Exploratory Data Analysis and Visualization in Data Science"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) is a critical step in the data science lifecycle. It involves inspecting datasets to summarize their main characteristics, often using statistical graphics and data visualization methods."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites and Setup"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before starting, ensure you have Python installed along with the core data science libraries: Pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, and Seaborn. You can install them using pip."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"pip install pandas numpy matplotlib seaborn"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Loading and Inspecting Data"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"The first step in EDA is loading your dataset into a Pandas DataFrame and inspecting its structure, data types, and missing values."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load dataset
df = pd.read_csv('dataset.csv')

# Display the first 5 rows
print(df.head())

# Check data types and missing values
print(df.info())"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary Statistics"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Generating summary statistics helps you understand the central tendency, dispersion, and shape of the dataset's distribution."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"# Generate descriptive statistics
print(df.describe())"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Univariate Analysis with Visualization"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Univariate analysis examines each variable separately. Histograms and box plots are ideal for visualizing the distribution of numerical features."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Set plotting style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Histogram for a specific numerical column
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
sns.histplot(df['age'], kde=True, bins=30)
plt.title('Age Distribution')
plt.xlabel('Age')
plt.ylabel('Count')
plt.show()"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Bivariate and Multivariate Analysis"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"To uncover relationships between multiple variables, use scatter plots, correlation matrices, and heatmaps."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"# Correlation matrix
corr_matrix = df.corr()

# Heatmap of correlations
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 8))
sns.heatmap(corr_matrix, annot=True, cmap="coolwarm", fmt=".2f")
plt.title('Feature Correlation Matrix')
plt.show()"},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for EDA"},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always check for missing values and handle them appropriately (imputation or removal)."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Identify and analyze outliers, as they can heavily skew machine learning models."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Keep visualizations clean and well-labeled with clear titles, axes, and legends."}]
